messages.text: Why does flow matching train faster than DDPM-style diffusion?
Flow matching regresses a velocity field along straight probability paths, so the target is simulation-free and has lower variance than score matching on curved paths.
And why does that matter for video models?
Straighter paths need fewer sampling steps, and fewer steps cut the cost of every frame a video model generates.

propositions.name: Flow matching
propositions.statement: Flow matching trains a network to regress the velocity field of a probability path from noise to data.

propositions.name: Straight paths
propositions.statement: Rectified flow paths between noise and data are close to straight lines.

propositions.name: Low-variance target
propositions.statement: A simulation-free regression target on straight paths has lower variance than score matching on curved paths.

propositions.name: Few sampling steps
propositions.statement: Straighter probability paths need fewer ODE solver steps at sampling time.

propositions.name: Cheaper video sampling
propositions.statement: Fewer sampling steps reduce the per-frame inference cost of a video generation model.
